themes_detail.label: Traffic Surge in East Flatbush
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints spiked to 3 reports last week—a 1100% increase from the 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—signaling a possible new congestion or illegal traffic pattern emerging in the district.
evidence: 3 traffic complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.35)
Spike appeared in the most recent reporting period (last week)
No prior news coverage or community board discussion of traffic issues
reporting_angles: What changed on East Flatbush streets last week? Interview DOT, local merchants, and residents about congestion patterns.
Are these complaints concentrated on specific corridors (e.g., Flatbush Ave, Church Ave)? Map the complaints.

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, Via) jumped to 4 reports last week—a 300% increase from the 1.0 weekly average—suggesting riders or residents are encountering new problems with app-based services in the district.
evidence: 4 for-hire vehicle complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.24)
Spike occurred in the most recent reporting week
No prior reporting on this issue in the district
reporting_angles: Talk to riders and drivers: Are fares surging? Are drivers refusing short trips? Are safety issues emerging?
Check with TLC on complaints filed directly and any enforcement actions in East Flatbush last week.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints rose to 22 reports last week—a 132% spike from the 9.5 weekly average—indicating a sustained sanitation problem that may be linked to the dumpster and root/sewer spikes also detected over the past 2 weeks.
evidence: 22 illegal dumping complaints last week vs. 9.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.57)
Dumpster complaints up 700% (4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 avg)
Root/sewer/sidewalk complaints up 180% (7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.5 avg) — suggests infrastructure strain
reporting_angles: Identify dumping hotspots: Are there specific blocks or intersections where complaints cluster? Walk them with a camera.
Interview DSNY about enforcement, staffing, and whether collection schedules have changed in East Flatbush.

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Concern (Historic Spike)
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints exploded to 3 reports 3 weeks ago—a 2300% increase from the 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69)—representing the largest anomaly in the district's recent 311 data, though the spike may have subsided; investigation needed to confirm if the issue resolved or reporting ceased.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69, highest statistical anomaly)
No follow-up complaints reported in the 2 weeks since, suggesting either resolution or reporting gap
Elevated heat/hot water complaints (3,448 over 90 days) may mask underlying water infrastructure issues
reporting_angles: FOIA request to DEP: Were there water main breaks, boil water advisories, or water testing anomalies in East Flatbush 3-4 weeks ago?
Interview residents from blocks where those 3 complaints originated—did they experience discoloration, taste, or odor issues? Did it persist?

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage and Root Damage Pattern
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked to 4 reports 2 weeks ago—a 967% increase from the 0.4 baseline—and root/sewer/sidewalk complaints rose 180% simultaneously, suggesting either a storm event, heavy construction activity, or coordinated infrastructure work that damaged trees and disrupted below-ground utilities.
evidence: 4 illegal tree damage complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.49)
7 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.4) — temporal overlap suggests connected cause
302 DOB permits filed over 90 days (172 alterations); unclear if spike coincides with major construction work
reporting_angles: Cross-reference DOB permits filed 3 weeks ago with the blocks where tree and root complaints originated—was construction ongoing?
Interview Parks Department and local elected officials: Were there storm damage assessments or tree-trimming operations 2 weeks ago?
